newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Nemtsov sees 1997 net grain crop 80 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Nemtsov sees 1997 net grain crop 80 mln T.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Thursday that Russia's net grain crop this year would be 80 million tonnes.

"This year, we expect a huge grain crop, especially in the Volga regions," he told reporters. "I believe the net crop will be 80 million tonnes." His forecast is above official government predictions of around 70 million tonnes.
Nemtsov, former governor of the Nizhny Novgorod region and a leading reformist, did not say why he thought output would rise above official predictions.
When asked about imports, he said: "We are not going to buy grain this year."
He was apparently referring to the fact that the government has not imported grain from world markets in recent years, and not to the fact that Russia's private wheat and wheatflour trade has soared.

Russia began its grain harvest in late June, hoping to better 1996's 69.3 million tonnes, which was the second worst crop in three decades. Declining consumption and lower livestock numbers have lessened the need for imported food and feed grains.
